The test image shows a tomato plant pulled from soil with:
- Stem cut open revealing white/cream interior
- White fungal growth at the stem base near soil line
- Completely dead plant with dried brown foliage
- Decay at stem base/crown area

This pattern suggests stem rot diseases. Top candidates: **Southern_Blight** (white mycelium at soil line), **Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot** (white cottony mycelium, internal decay), or possibly **Southern_Bacterial_Wilt**.

Let me view reference images systematically — one per class.
Good match — Southern_Blight shows white mycelium at stem base, very similar to test image. Now checking Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot.
Sclerotinia reference shows sclerotia closeup — less relevant to test image. Checking Southern_Bacterial_Wilt next.
Southern_Bacterial_Wilt shows bacterial streaming test — not a match. Checking Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot (stem view) and Bacterial_Wilt in parallel.
Sclerotinia shows wilted plants but no white mycelium at soil line like test image. Now checking Bacterial_Wilt, Alternaria, and Phytophthora_Blight.
Need one more class. Checking Verticillium_Wilt (also causes whole-plant death).

All 8 reference views complete. Summary of comparisons:

| Class | Match to Test Image |
|-------|-------------------|
| **Southern_Blight** | **STRONG** — white mycelium at stem base, dead plant pulled from soil |
| Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot | Weak — sclerotia closeup, wilted plants; no white soil-line mycelium |
| Southern_Bacterial_Wilt | No — bacterial streaming test, different presentation |
| Bacterial_Wilt | No — bacterial streaming test |
| Alternaria_Black_Molds_Stem_Cankers | No — dark canker, not white mycelium |
| Phytophthora_Blight | No — dark blackened stems |
| Verticillium_Wilt | No — leaf yellowing, no stem-base symptoms |

**Conclusion:** The test image shows a tomato plant pulled from sandy soil with prominent **white cottony mycelium at the stem base/crown**, a cut stem with white interior, and completely dead foliage. This is the hallmark of *Sclerotium rolfsii* (Southern Blight). The Southern_Blight reference (Bugwood_2) is nearly identical in presentation — white mycelial growth on the stem near soil line, dead plant, similar soil type.
